overview: The Eastern Han restored the dynasty after Wang Mang's interregnum, ruling from the eastern capital at Luoyang. This period saw continued technological innovation, the spread of Buddhism and growing power of eunuchs and landed families.

items.text: Cai Lun perfects papermaking, making paper cheap and widely available.
The first true porcelain produced in China, though it remained rare.
Xu Shen compiles the Shuowen Jiezi, the first comprehensive Chinese dictionary analyzing character etymology.
Emperor Ming dreams of the Buddha and sends envoys to India, beginning official Buddhist patronage.
Daoism develops as an organized religion alongside philosophical Daoism.
Paper becomes the primary writing medium, enabling the spread of literacy and bureaucracy.
Buddhism takes root in China, eventually becoming a major religion.

fall.text: The last Han emperor abdicated to Cao Pi, who founded the Cao Wei dynasty and began the Three Kingdoms period.
